[AtlantECO](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/metagenomics/super-studies/atlanteco) brings
together studies of the Atlantic Ocean and its ecosystems. Fetch samples from
all its flagship studies and explore their locations on a map.

Edit and run the cells in order. The first visit may take a minute to load.

## Find the studies

A super-study groups related MGnify studies. Show the first 20 AtlantECO flagship studies. Change `20` to see more:

```{pyodide}
import requests
import pandas as pd
import folium
from html import escape

API = "https://www.ebi.ac.uk/metagenomics/api/v2"

def get_json(path, **params):
    response = requests.get(f"{API}/{path}", params=params, timeout=30)
    response.raise_for_status()
    return response.json()

atlanteco = get_json("super-studies/atlanteco")
studies = pd.DataFrame(atlanteco["flagship_studies"])
study_titles = dict(zip(studies["accession"], studies["title"]))
studies[["accession", "title"]].head(20)
```

## Get the samples

Collect every page of samples for each flagship study. A sample can belong to
several studies, so keep one record per sample accession. Unavailable studies
are reported and skipped.

```{pyodide}
samples_by_accession = {}
sample_studies = {}
for study_accession in studies["accession"]:
    page = 1
    while True:
        try:
            batch = get_json(f"studies/{study_accession}/samples/", page=page, page_size=1000)
        except requests.HTTPError as error:
            if error.response.status_code != 404:
                raise
            print(f"{study_accession}: samples unavailable; skipped")
            break
        for sample in batch["items"]:
            samples_by_accession[sample["accession"]] = sample
            sample_studies.setdefault(sample["accession"], set()).add(study_accession)
        if not batch["items"] or page * 1000 >= batch["count"]:
            print(f"{study_accession}: {batch['count']} samples")
            break
        page += 1

samples = list(samples_by_accession.values())
print(f"Fetched {len(samples)} unique samples from {len(studies)} listed studies")
```

## Prepare the coordinates

Latitude and longitude are stored in the sample metadata as text. Convert them
to numbers and omit samples with missing or out-of-range coordinates.

```{pyodide}
locations = pd.json_normalize(samples).reindex(
    columns=["accession", "metadata.lat", "metadata.lon"]
).rename(columns={"metadata.lat": "latitude", "metadata.lon": "longitude"})

for column in ["latitude", "longitude"]:
    locations[column] = pd.to_numeric(locations[column], errors="coerce")

locations = locations[
    locations["latitude"].between(-90, 90)
    & locations["longitude"].between(-180, 180)
]
locations["study_accessions"] = locations["accession"].map(
    lambda accession: sorted(sample_studies.get(accession, []))
)
print(f"Mapping {len(locations)} of {len(samples)} samples")
locations.head()
```

## Draw the map

Zoom in and click a marker to see the sample accession, the AtlantECO studies it
belongs to, and its coordinates. Samples collected at the same location share a
marker position.

```{pyodide}
if locations.empty:
    raise ValueError("No samples have usable coordinates.")

sample_map = folium.Map(tiles="OpenStreetMap", prefer_canvas=True)
for sample in locations.itertuples(index=False):
    study_lines = "<br>".join(
        f"{escape(accession)}: {escape(study_titles.get(accession, ''))}"
        for accession in sample.study_accessions
    )
    popup = folium.Popup(
        "<b>Sample:</b> " + escape(sample.accession)
        + "<br><b>Studies:</b><br>" + study_lines
        + f"<br><b>Coordinates:</b> {sample.latitude:.4f}, {sample.longitude:.4f}",
        max_width=360,
    )
    folium.CircleMarker(
        location=[sample.latitude, sample.longitude],
        radius=3,
        popup=popup,
        color="#007c80",
        fill=True,
        fill_opacity=0.7,
    ).add_to(sample_map)

sample_map.fit_bounds(locations[["latitude", "longitude"]].values.tolist(), max_zoom=10)
sample_map
```

Try changing the marker colour or radius, then run the map cell again.

## Running this code in your own environment

Install the packages from a terminal:

```bash
python -m pip install pandas requests folium
```

Run the Python cells in a notebook to display the map. In a Python script,
use `sample_map.save("atlanteco.html")` and open that file in your browser.
